newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S HARYANA EYES 12 PERCENT INDUSTRIAL GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S HARYANA EYES 12 PERCENT INDUSTRIAL GROWTH.

text.p: The northern Indian state of Haryana said on Tuesday that it hopes to achieve 12 percent annual industrial growth over the next five years.
The state cabinet approved a new economic policy that seeks to increase industrial growth to 12 percent from 7.7 percent achieved in 1996/97 (April-March).
The policy also aims to raise the share of industry in state's domestic product to 30 percent from 24 percent.
It seeks to increase private sector participation in the development of infrastructure, with special emphasis on power and telecommunications.
The state relaxed the period of payment of sales tax by industries to seven years. At present industries are required to pay sales tax after five years from the date of first sale.
The policy also announced a special provision for immediate allotment of land to industrial units which propose an investment of more than 500 million rupees in the state.
